title: PIP's Halloween Pop-up Shop: a cute Halloween game I made with AI tools so my kids could play
author: aaron_tseng
selftext:
Halloween is coming, and I wanted to give kids a cute game for it.

A costume pop-up at a Seattle mall sparked it: fun costumes and props, even scary stuff. It felt slightly creepy, with a surprise around every corner. I pictured Halloween from a bystander's view. Mechanics kept growing and the direction drifted. I wanted it scarier, but Halloween should be fun for kids. I wanted my own kids to play, so a cute costume shop won. Time was short, so it went warmer and cuter. I hope to do better next year.

Help little demon PIP run a Halloween costume shop, picking costumes from customers' clues. It's free in the browser, in English and Traditional Chinese, with a short tutorial showing the basics.

I made the game with AI tools. I directed it and playtested. Claude wrote the code and tests, and also handled the translation. Codex drew the characters and scenes and drafted the store-page copy. Google Gemini generated the music.

One thing that stuck with me: Dr. Crow, the town doctor, had human mouth lines drawn on his beak in all 4 pictures. Every automated check and several rounds of AI visual review missed them. I finally noticed while looking at a screenshot.

How do you catch visual mistakes that survive your automated checks and AI reviews?

🎃 Play here: https://amiejm.itch.io/pips-halloween-popup-shop  
Teaser: https://youtu.be/eLLKrWaWzf4  
Full soundtrack: https://youtu.be/IEPF\_XOWbxU

Views are my own.
